comments.comment: Hi qian_wc could you please have a look?

sanity test 123k hit the same issue:
https://testing.whamcloud.com/test_sets/88069434-45dd-4b38-a1cf-2f1d744bd519

The failure occurred consistently:
https://testing.whamcloud.com/test_sets/88cb44b6-141b-40e0-850f-fba3ecbd05aa

I‘ve seen the problem and found a very possible reason.

First of all, on both OS, Ubuntu 26.04 and Rocky 9, they have the same output when readdir.

strace -v -e getdents64 du -a /mnt/lustre/test_123h > /tmp/strace_getdents64_du.log 2>&1
getdents64(3, [{d_ino=144115205289280029, d_off=4294967296, d_reclen=24, d_type=DT_DIR, d_name="."}, {d_ino=144115188193296385, d_off=36452015458850, d_reclen=24, d_type=DT_DIR, d_name=".."}, {d_ino=144115205306059211, d_off=1532455491355451, d_reclen=24, d_type=DT_REG, d_name="1477"}, {d_ino=144115205306061086, d_off=1652055103461130, d_reclen=24, d_type=DT_REG, d_name="3352"}
......

But they Do have a difference after readdir.

This is Rocky 9's realization. 

readdir({ 3 })                                   = { 144115205306066424, "8690" }
strlen("8690")                                   = 4

fstatat(4, 0x555764c9bf90, 0x555764c9bf00, 256)  = 0

It begins with filename "0", then "1" "2" and so on.

And the fstatat() call in the log will trigger the readahead thread. It will take in filename "0" "1" "2" ...... in sequence, which will disabled the list_pattern check and enabled a fname pattern.

But on Ubuntu 26.04, it looks like this.

readdir({3})                                     = {144115205306066424, "8690"}

) = 0
memmove(0x6102a52c16e6, "3352\0", 5)             = 0x6102a52c16e6
fstatat(4, "3352", 0x6102a52c3050, 0b100000000)  = 0
localeconv(0, 0x6102a52c16d0, 0, 0)              = 0x75c072e13880
strlen(".")                                      = 1
strlen(",")                                      = 1
fputs_unlocked("0", 0x75c072e13580)              = 1
__printf_chk(2, "\t%s%c", "/mnt/lustre/test_123h/3352", '\n') = 28
fflush_unlocked(0x75c072e13580, 0x7ffc38559561, 0, 00   /mnt/lustre/test_123h/3352
) = 0

It will output the file name in the sequence exactly as they were read out of the dir, without a sort, "1477" "3352" and so on. 

This will enable the list pattern of readahead thread and skip the fname pattern check,

The lproc output "fname_total" will remain 0, and fails the test.

And I found this, 

https://lists.gnu.org/archive/html/bug-coreutils/2025-12/msg00026.html

It seems it's our own request make the GNU did this change?

And maybe we should let Tim know about this?

yujian Currently I don't think the problem is fatal.

In Ubuntu 26.04, "du" just can not trigger fname pattern and I don't know if there is any way to do so.

But even with list pattern, the hit rate remains good.

Maybe just skip the test_123h for Ubuntu 26.04.
This is caused by behavior change of "du" command. Re-assigned to Wang Xiyang to fix.

Confirmed it comes from following patch:

coreutils (9.7-3ubuntu2) resolute; urgency=medium
  * Fix slow performance of 'du' on large directories (>= 10K files)
    on Lustre filesystems by skipping inode sorting. The default
    behaviour of sorting dirents by inode numbers negatively impacts
    performance on Lustre because it interferes with Lustre's ability
    to prefetch file metadata via statahead. (LP: #2137373)
    - d/p/lp2137373-skip-dirent-inode-sorting-for-lustre.patch
 -- Munir Siddiqui <munir.siddiqui@canonical.com>  Fri, 23 Jan 2026 18:41:52 +0500

And the patch was fixed in gnulib without a interface to tune.
